ESV.1: Now a man from the house of Levi went and took as his wife a Levite woman.
ESV.2: The woman conceived and bore a son, and when she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.
ESV.3: When she could hide him no longer, she took for him a basket made of bulrushes  and daubed it with bitumen and pitch. She put the child in it and placed it among the reeds by the river bank.
ESV.4: And his sister stood at a distance to know what would be done to him.
ESV.5: Now the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the river, while her young women walked beside the river. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her servant woman, and she took it.
ESV.6: When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the baby was crying. She took pity on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrews' children.”
ESV.7: Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, “Shall I go and call you a nurse from the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?”
ESV.8: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her, “Go.” So the girl went and called the child's mother.
ESV.9: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her, “Take this child away and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages.” So the woman took the child and nursed him.
ESV.10: When the child grew older, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, “Because,” she said, “I drew him out of the water.”
ESV.11: One day, when Moses had grown up, he went out to his people and looked on their burdens, and he saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his people.
ESV.12: He looked this way and that, and seeing no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.
ESV.13: When he went out the next day, behold, two Hebrews were struggling together. And he said to the man in the wrong, “Why do you strike your companion?”
ESV.14: He answered, “Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you mean to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?” Then Moses was afraid, and thought, “Surely the thing is known.”
ESV.15: When Pharaoh heard of it, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and stayed in the land of Midian. And he sat down by a well.
ESV.16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came and drew water and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
ESV.17: The shepherds came and drove them away, but Moses stood up and saved them, and watered their flock.
ESV.18: When they came home to their father Reuel, he said, “How is it that you have come home so soon today?”
ESV.19: They said, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds and even drew water for us and watered the flock.”
ESV.20: He said to his daughters, “Then where is he? Why have you left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.”
ESV.21: And Moses was content to dwell with the man, and he gave Moses his daughter Zipporah.
ESV.22: She gave birth to a son, and he called his name Gershom, for he said, “I have been a sojourner  in a foreign land.”
ESV.23: During those many days the king of Egypt died, and the people of Israel groaned because of their slavery and cried out for help. Their cry for rescue from slavery came up to God.
ESV.24: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
ESV.25: God saw the people of Israel — and God knew.

NASB.1: Now a man from the house of Levi went and married a daughter of Levi.
NASB.2: The woman conceived and bore a son; and when she saw that he was beautiful, she hid him for three months.
NASB.3: But when she could hide him no longer, she got him a wicker basket and covered it over with tar and pitch. Then she put the child into it and set [it] among the reeds by the bank of the Nile.
NASB.4: His sister stood at a distance to find out what would happen to him.
NASB.5: The daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the Nile, with her maidens walking alongside the Nile; and she saw the basket among the reeds and sent her maid, and she brought it [to her].
NASB.6: When she opened [it], she saw the child, and behold, [the] boy was crying. And she had pity on him and said, 'This is one of the Hebrews' children.'
NASB.7: Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, 'Shall I go and call a nurse for you from the Hebrew women that she may nurse the child for you?'
NASB.8: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, 'Go [ahead].' So the girl went and called the child's mother.
NASB.9: Then Pharaoh's daughter said to her, 'Take this child away and nurse him for me and I will give [you] your wages.' So the woman took the child and nursed him.
NASB.10: The child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter and he became her son. And she named him Moses, and said, 'Because I drew him out of the water.'
NASB.11: Now it came about in those days, when Moses had grown up, that he went out to his brethren and looked on their hard labors; and he saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his brethren.
NASB.12: So he looked this way and that, and when he saw there was no one [around], he struck down the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.
NASB.13: He went out the next day, and behold, two Hebrews were fighting with each other; and he said to the offender, 'Why are you striking your companion?'
NASB.14: But he said, 'Who made you a prince or a judge over us? Are you intending to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?' Then Moses was afraid and said, 'Surely the matter has become known.'
NASB.15: When Pharaoh heard of this matter, he tried to kill Moses. But Moses fled from the presence of Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, and he sat down by a well.
NASB.16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters; and they came to draw water and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
NASB.17: Then the shepherds came and drove them away, but Moses stood up and helped them and watered their flock.
NASB.18: When they came to Reuel their father, he said, 'Why have you come [back] so soon today?'
NASB.19: So they said, 'An Egyptian delivered us from the hand of the shepherds, and what is more, he even drew the water for us and watered the flock.'
NASB.20: He said to his daughters, 'Where is he then? Why is it that you have left the man behind? Invite him to have something to eat.'
NASB.21: Moses was willing to dwell with the man, and he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses.
NASB.22: Then she gave birth to a son, and he named him Gershom, for he said, 'I have been a sojourner in a foreign land.'
NASB.23: Now it came about in [the course of] those many days that the king of Egypt died. And the sons of Israel sighed because of the bondage, and they cried out; and their cry for help because of [their] bondage rose up to God.
NASB.24: So God heard their groaning; and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
NASB.25: God saw the sons of Israel, and God took notice [of them].

WEB.1: A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.
WEB.2: The woman conceived, and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.
WEB.3: When she could no longer hide him, she took a papyrus basket for him, and coated it with tar and with pitch. She put the child in it, and laid it in the reeds by the river’s bank.
WEB.4: His sister stood far off, to see what would be done to him.
WEB.5: Pharaoh’s daughter came down to bathe at the river. Her maidens walked along by the riverside. She saw the basket among the reeds, and sent her servant to get it.
WEB.6: She opened it, and saw the child, and behold, the baby cried. She had compassion on him, and said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.”
WEB.7: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Should I go and call a nurse for you from the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for you?”
WEB.8: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Go.” The maiden went and called the child’s mother.
WEB.9: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child away, and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages.” The woman took the child, and nursed it.
WEB.10: The child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses,  and said, “Because I drew him out of the water.”
WEB.11: In those days, when Moses had grown up, he went out to his brothers, and looked at their burdens. He saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, one of his brothers.
WEB.12: He looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no one, he killed the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
WEB.13: He went out the second day, and behold, two men of the Hebrews were fighting with each other. He said to him who did the wrong, “Why do you strike your fellow?”
WEB.14: He said, “Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you plan to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian?” Moses was afraid, and said, “Surely this thing is known.”
WEB.15: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and lived in the land of Midian, and he sat down by a well.
WEB.16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.
WEB.17: The shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
WEB.18: When they came to Reuel, their father, he said, “How is it that you have returned so early today?”
WEB.19: They said, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and moreover he drew water for us, and watered the flock.”
WEB.20: He said to his daughters, “Where is he? Why is it that you have left the man? Call him, that he may eat bread.”
WEB.21: Moses was content to dwell with the man. He gave Moses Zipporah, his daughter.
WEB.22: She bore a son, and he named him Gershom,  for he said, “I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land.”
WEB.23: In the course of those many days, the king of Egypt died, and the children of Israel sighed because of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up to God because of the bondage.
WEB.24: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
WEB.25: God saw the children of Israel, and God was concerned about them.

AMP.1: Now a man of the house of Levi [the priestly tribe] went and took as his wife a daughter of Levi.
AMP.2: The woman conceived and gave birth to a son; and when she saw that he was [especially] beautiful and healthy, she hid him for three months [to protect him from the Egyptians].
AMP.3: When she could no longer hide him, she got him a basket (chest) made of papyrus reeds and covered it with tar and pitch [making it waterproof]. Then she put the child in it and set it among the reeds by the bank of the Nile.
AMP.4: And his sister [Miriam] stood some distance away to find out what would happen to him.
AMP.5: Now the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the Nile, and [she, together with] her maidens walked along the river's bank; she saw the basket among the reeds and sent her maid [to get it], and she brought it to her.
AMP.6: When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the baby was crying. And she took pity on him and said, "This is one of the Hebrews' children."
AMP.7: Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, "Shall I go and call a wet-nurse from the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?"
AMP.8: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Go ahead." So the girl went and called the child's mother.
AMP.9: Then Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Take this child away and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages." So the woman took the child and nursed him.
AMP.10: And the child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter and he became her son. And she named him Moses, and said, "Because I drew him out of the water."
AMP.11: One day, after Moses had grown [into adulthood], it happened that he went to his countrymen and looked [with compassion] at their hard labors; and he saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his countrymen.
AMP.12: He turned to look around, and seeing no one, he killed the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.
AMP.13: He went out the next day and saw two Hebrew men fighting with each other; and he said to the aggressor, "Why are you striking your friend?"
AMP.14: But the man said, "Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you intend to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?" Then Moses was afraid and said, "Certainly this incident is known."
AMP.15: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he tried to kill Moses. Then Moses fled from Pharaoh's presence and took refuge in the land of Midian, where he sat down by a well.
AMP.16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters; and they came and drew water [from the well where Moses was resting] and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
AMP.17: Then shepherds came and drove them away, but Moses stood up and helped them and watered their flock.
AMP.18: When they came to Reuel (Jethro) their father, he said, "How is it that you have come back so soon today?"
AMP.19: They said, "An Egyptian saved us from the shepherds. He even drew water [from the well] for us and watered the flock."
AMP.20: Then he said to his daughters, "Where is he? Why have you left the man behind? Invite him to have something to eat."
AMP.21: Moses was willing to remain with the man, and he gave Moses his daughter Zipporah [to be his wife].
AMP.22: She gave birth to a son, and he named him Gershom (stranger); for he said, "I have been a stranger in a foreign land."
AMP.23: Now it happened after a long time [about forty years] that the king of Egypt died. And the children of Israel (Jacob) groaned and sighed because of the bondage, and they cried out. And their cry for help because of their bondage ascended to God.
AMP.24: So God heard their groaning and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (Israel).
AMP.25: God saw the sons of Israel, and God took notice [of them] and was concerned about them [knowing all, understanding all, remembering all].

NLT.1: About this time, a man and woman from the tribe of Levi got married.
NLT.2: The woman became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She saw that he was a special baby and kept him hidden for three months.
NLT.3: But when she could no longer hide him, she got a basket made of papyrus reeds and waterproofed it with tar and pitch. She put the baby in the basket and laid it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile River.
NLT.4: The baby’s sister then stood at a distance, watching to see what would happen to him.
NLT.5: Soon Pharaoh’s daughter came down to bathe in the river, and her attendants walked along the riverbank. When the princess saw the basket among the reeds, she sent her maid to get it for her.
NLT.6: When the princess opened it, she saw the baby. The little boy was crying, and she felt sorry for him. “This must be one of the Hebrew children,” she said.
NLT.7: Then the baby’s sister approached the princess. “Should I go and find one of the Hebrew women to nurse the baby for you?” she asked.
NLT.8: “Yes, do!” the princess replied. So the girl went and called the baby’s mother.
NLT.9: “Take this baby and nurse him for me,” the princess told the baby’s mother. “I will pay you for your help.” So the woman took her baby home and nursed him.
NLT.10: Later, when the boy was older, his mother brought him back to Pharaoh’s daughter, who adopted him as her own son. The princess named him Moses, for she explained, “I lifted him out of the water.”
NLT.11: Many years later, when Moses had grown up, he went out to visit his own people, the Hebrews, and he saw how hard they were forced to work. During his visit, he saw an Egyptian beating one of his fellow Hebrews.
NLT.12: After looking in all directions to make sure no one was watching, Moses killed the Egyptian and hid the body in the sand.
NLT.13: The next day, when Moses went out to visit his people again, he saw two Hebrew men fighting. “Why are you beating up your friend?” Moses said to the one who had started the fight.
NLT.14: The man replied, “Who appointed you to be our prince and judge? Are you going to kill me as you killed that Egyptian yesterday?” Then Moses was afraid, thinking, “Everyone knows what I did.”
NLT.15: And sure enough, Pharaoh heard what had happened, and he tried to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and went to live in the land of Midian. When Moses arrived in Midian, he sat down beside a well.
NLT.16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters who came as usual to draw water and fill the water troughs for their father’s flocks.
NLT.17: But some other shepherds came and chased them away. So Moses jumped up and rescued the girls from the shepherds. Then he drew water for their flocks.
NLT.18: When the girls returned to Reuel, their father, he asked, “Why are you back so soon today?”
NLT.19: “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds,” they answered. “And then he drew water for us and watered our flocks.”
NLT.20: “Then where is he?” their father asked. “Why did you leave him there? Invite him to come and eat with us.”
NLT.21: Moses accepted the invitation, and he settled there with him. In time, Reuel gave Moses his daughter Zipporah to be his wife.
NLT.22: Later she gave birth to a son, and Moses named him Gershom, for he explained, “I have been a foreigner in a foreign land.”
NLT.23: Years passed, and the king of Egypt died. But the Israelites continued to groan under their burden of slavery. They cried out for help, and their cry rose up to God.
NLT.24: God heard their groaning, and he remembered his covenant promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
NLT.25: He looked down on the people of Israel and knew it was time to act.

NIV.1:
The Birth of Moses

NIV.2: and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him for three months.
NIV.3: But when she could hide him no longer, she got a papyrus basket for him and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in it and put it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.
NIV.4: His sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.
NIV.5: Then Pharaoh’s daughter went down to the Nile to bathe, and her attendants were walking along the river bank. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her slave girl to get it.
NIV.6: She opened it and saw the baby. He was crying, and she felt sorry for him. “This is one of the Hebrew babies,” she said.
NIV.7: Then his sister asked Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and get one of the Hebrew women to nurse the baby for you?”
NIV.8: “Yes, go,” she answered. And the girl went and got the baby’s mother.
NIV.9: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this baby and nurse him for me, and I will pay you.” So the woman took the baby and nursed him.
NIV.10: When the child grew older, she took him to Pharaoh’s daughter and he became her son. She named him Moses, saying, “I drew him out of the water.”
NIV.11:
Moses Flees to Midian
One day, after Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were and watched them at their hard labor. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.
NIV.12: Glancing this way and that and seeing no one, he killed the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.
NIV.13: The next day he went out and saw two Hebrews fighting. He asked the one in the wrong, “Why are you hitting your fellow Hebrew?”
NIV.14: The man said, “Who made you ruler and judge over us? Are you thinking of killing me as you killed the Egyptian?” Then Moses was afraid and thought, “What I did must have become known.”
NIV.15: When Pharaoh heard of this, he tried to kill Moses, but Moses fled from Pharaoh and went to live in Midian, where he sat down by a well.
NIV.16: Now a priest of Midian had seven daughters, and they came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father’s flock.
NIV.17: Some shepherds came along and drove them away, but Moses got up and came to their rescue and watered their flock.

MSG.1: A man from the family of Levi married a Levite woman.
MSG.2: The woman became pregnant and had a son. She saw there was something special about him and hid him. She hid him for three months.
MSG.3: When she couldn't hide him any longer she got a little basket-boat made of papyrus, waterproofed it with tar and pitch, and placed the child in it. Then she set it afloat in the reeds at the edge of the Nile.
MSG.4: The baby's older sister found herself a vantage point a little way off and watched to see what would happen to him.
MSG.5: Pharaoh's daughter came down to the Nile to bathe; her maidens strolled on the bank. She saw the basket-boat floating in the reeds and sent her maid to get it.
MSG.6: She opened it and saw the child—a baby crying! Her heart went out to him. She said, "This must be one of the Hebrew babies."
MSG.7: Then his sister was before her: "Do you want me to go and get a nursing mother from the Hebrews so she can nurse the baby for you?"
MSG.8: Pharaoh's daughter said, "Yes. Go." The girl went and called the child's mother.
MSG.9: Pharaoh's daughter told her, "Take this baby and nurse him for me. I'll pay you." The woman took the child and nursed him.
MSG.10: After the child was weaned, she presented him to Pharaoh's daughter who adopted him as her son. She named him Moses (Pulled-Out), saying, "I pulled him out of the water."
MSG.11: Time passed. Moses grew up. One day he went and saw his brothers, saw all that hard labor. Then he saw an Egyptian hit a Hebrew—one of his relatives!
MSG.12: He looked this way and then that; when he realized there was no one in sight, he killed the Egyptian and buried him in the sand.
MSG.13: The next day he went out there again. Two Hebrew men were fighting. He spoke to the man who started it: "Why are you hitting your neighbor?"
MSG.14:
The man shot back: "Who do you think you are, telling us what to do? Are you going to kill me the way you killed that Egyptian?"
Then Moses panicked: "Word's gotten out—people know about this."
MSG.15: Pharaoh heard about it and tried to kill Moses, but Moses got away to the land of Midian. He sat down by a well.
MSG.16: The priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came and drew water, filling the troughs and watering their father's sheep.
MSG.17: When some shepherds came and chased the girls off, Moses came to their rescue and helped them water their sheep.
MSG.18: When they got home to their father, Reuel, he said, "That didn't take long. Why are you back so soon?"
MSG.19: "An Egyptian," they said, "rescued us from a bunch of shepherds. Why, he even drew water for us and watered the sheep."
MSG.20: He said, "So where is he? Why did you leave him behind? Invite him so he can have something to eat with us."
MSG.21: Moses agreed to settle down there with the man, who then gave his daughter Zipporah (Bird) to him for his wife.
MSG.22: She had a son, and Moses named him Gershom (Sojourner), saying, "I'm a sojourner in a foreign country."
MSG.23: Many years later the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned under their slavery and cried out. Their cries for relief from their hard labor ascended to God:
MSG.24:
God listened to their groanings.
God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
MSG.25:
God saw what was going on with Israel.
God understood.
